title: Docs: say what a kind's battery is, in one place
body:
### Where?

`kinds/README.md` (the opening paragraph and the `workflows` row of the `pack.yml` table), and the other places that say "battery" without saying what it is: `docs/adopting.md`, `docs/configuration.md` (`workflows` row), `docs/maintaining.md`, the comments of `kinds/*/pack.yml`, `.github/workflows/plugin-checks-wp.yml` and `scripts/sync-repos.py` (`kind_battery()` and its `callers` doc header).

### What is missing, wrong or unclear?

"Battery" (a kind's battery, "ready for the battery") is used across the docs, the packs and the scripts, but no page says what it means. A maintainer reading the autopilot's question on #684 ("where 'ready for the battery' is read from") could not tell what it referred to. The closest is the opening paragraph of `kinds/README.md` ("the list of workflows that make up its battery"), which uses the word as if it were already known, and does not say how the battery differs from the workflows every repository gets, nor that a repository gets the caller that runs it.

### Proposed solution

One definition, in one place, that every other mention links to: in `kinds/README.md`, under "What a pack holds" or as a short "Words" paragraph near the top, say that a kind's battery is the set of reusable workflows that check, test, release and publish a repository of that kind (pack.yml `workflows`, for wordpress-plugin plugin-checks-wp.yml, plugin-tests-wp.yml, plugin-release-wp.yml and plugin-publish-wp.yml); that it is distinct from the workflows every repository gets whatever its kind (repos.yml `every-repository`: conventions, review, pull-request comments); that a repository runs it through its callers, the small files in its own `.github/workflows/` that `scripts/sync-repos.py callers` writes from `workflow-templates/`; and what "ready for the battery" means once #681 settles it (the files the battery needs at the repository's root). The `workflows` rows of `kinds/README.md` and `docs/configuration.md`, and `docs/adopting.md`, link to that definition instead of repeating the word bare. If `docs/model.md` keeps a glossary, the term goes there with a link to the same place.

### Problem

A word that only the people who wrote the engine understand makes the autopilot's questions, the drift report and the docs unreadable to everyone else, the maintainer included, and an answer given without understanding the question is a decision taken blind.

### Scope

`kinds/README.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/adopting.md`, `docs/maintaining.md`, and `docs/model.md` only if it has a glossary. Words only: no workflow, script or pack changes.

### Out of scope

What "ready for the battery" checks and where it is read from, which #681 decides. Renaming the term.

### Acceptance criteria

C1: Given `kinds/README.md`, when a reader looks for what a battery is, then one paragraph defines it, names the pack key it comes from (`workflows`), gives the wordpress-plugin example, and says how it differs from the workflows every repository gets and how a repository runs it (its callers).
C2: Given `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/adopting.md` and `docs/maintaining.md`, when they say "battery", then the first mention on each page links to that definition.

### Criticality

Normal

### Who works on it

- [ ] I want to work on this myself

🤖 AI-assisted · Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)

### Spec: approach

Add a short section `## The battery` to `kinds/README.md`, right after the `pack.yml` table in "What a pack holds" (its heading gives the stable anchor `#the-battery`), holding one paragraph that says: a kind's battery is the reusable workflows in `.github/workflows/` that check, test, release and publish a repository of that kind, as listed under the pack's `workflows` key; for wordpress-plugin, `plugin-checks-wp.yml`, `plugin-tests-wp.yml`, `plugin-release-wp.yml` and `plugin-publish-wp.yml`; it differs from the workflows every repository gets whatever its kind (`repos.yml` `every-repository`: `issues.yml`, `pull-request-comments.yml`, and `org-pull-request.yml` that the organisation's ruleset requires) because only a repository of that kind gets it; and a repository runs it through its callers, the files from `workflow-templates/` that `sync-repos.py callers` writes into its `.github/workflows/` and that name the battery's workflows (GitHub cannot pick a reusable workflow from data). The earlier mentions in `kinds/README.md` (intro, the `workflows` row) link to that section.

In `docs/adopting.md` and `docs/maintaining.md`, the first "battery" on each page becomes a link to `../kinds/README.md#the-battery`. `docs/configuration.md` is generated by `scripts/settings.py docs` from `policy/settings-schema.yml` (`test_configuration_doc.py` fails a hand edit), so the link goes into the `says:` of the `workflows` setting there and the page is regenerated with `python3 scripts/settings.py docs > docs/configuration.md`. That is a change of words in a data file under `policy/`, not of a workflow, script or pack; `docs/model.md` has no glossary and no "battery", so it is left alone. Nothing widens any permission, secret, lane or limit.

### Spec: files

- kinds/README.md
- docs/adopting.md
- docs/maintaining.md
- policy/settings-schema.yml (the `says:` of the `workflows` setting only)
- docs/configuration.md (regenerated)
- tests/workflows/test_battery_doc.py (new)

### Spec: tests

- C1 → tests/workflows/test_battery_doc.py
- C2 → tests/workflows/test_battery_doc.py

title: fix: the autopilot's own last pushes cancel its review
body:
### What happened?

The Claude review of an autopilot pull request is cancelled when the autopilot ends a round, and the autopilot then stops with "the review job failed with an empty log" and `needs-human`. On #810 the autopilot pushed 28b8aec4 and, six seconds later, its "chore: ready for review" commit 6fb2fccd while marking the pull request ready: runs 44043703798, 44043761359 and 44043777103 started within 30 seconds, the review of 44043761359 failed and the review of 44043777103 ended "The operation was canceled." after 31 seconds. The same stop hit #800 (run 43985176591) and #812 (run 44014031620, and again on its re-run), and each needed a person to re-run the review or ask for another push.

### Steps to reproduce

Let the autopilot finish a round on a pull request: it pushes its last commit, pushes "chore: ready for review" and marks the pull request ready within seconds. The review job's concurrency group (`claude-review-<repo>-<number>-code`, `cancel-in-progress: true`, .github/workflows/claude-review.yml) cancels the earlier review, and the stop step reads the cancelled or failed review as a review failure.

### Version

v7.15.1

### Proposed solution

A review cancelled by a newer run of the same pull request is not a failure: the autopilot's stop step ignores a cancelled review when a newer review run of the same head or a later one exists, and waits for that one. The autopilot ends its round with one push, the ready commit included, so a round starts one review.

### Problem

A review cancelled by the autopilot's own last pushes is read as a failed review, so the autopilot hands the pull request to a person who only has to re-run it, several times a night.

### Scope

- The autopilot's stop step tells a review cancelled by a newer run from a failed one, and waits for the newer run.
- The autopilot's round ends with a single push that includes the ready commit.
- A test that would have caught it.

### Out of scope

- The review's own concurrency group and what the review checks.

### Acceptance criteria

- C1: Given an autopilot pull request whose review run was cancelled by a newer run of the same pull request, when the autopilot reads the review's result, then it does not stop with `needs-human` and waits for the newer run's review.
- C2: Given the autopilot ending a round, when it marks the pull request ready, then its last commits reach the branch in one push and one review run starts.
- C3: Given a review that fails on its own (not cancelled), when the autopilot reads it, then it stops as it does today.

### Criticality

Normal

🤖 AI-generated · Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)

### Spec: approach

Two causes, two changes, both in the engine.

C1/C3, the stop. When a run's review is cancelled, the pipeline's `autopilot-fix` job still calls autopilot.yml in `fix` mode. A check round then hands the agent the log of a cancelled job, and the agent stops with `finish stop` ("change nothing… so a person runs it again"), which adds `needs-human`. The fix: a new pure function in scripts/autopilot.py, `superseded(run_id, run_head, pr_head, review_conclusion, newer_runs)`, with a command `autopilot.py superseded` that reads its inputs from the API. The command reads this run's jobs (GITHUB_RUN_ID), the PR's head, and the pipeline's runs for the PR's branch. It exits 0 and says why when a newer run supersedes this one: the PR's head has moved past the commit this run checked (RUN_HEAD, from `github.event.pull_request.head.sha`, passed in by the prep job), or the review job's conclusion is `cancelled` and a newer run of the same workflow exists for the PR. It exits 1 when nothing supersedes the run, and 2 when it cannot read the inputs. In prep's "may" step, `fix` mode (not the merge queue's round), it runs before the rounds cap. If the run is superseded, the step logs "waits for the newer run's review", sets go=false and exits: no round is counted, no agent runs, nothing is commented, no label is added. The newer run's own `autopilot-fix` acts on its review. On exit 1 or 2 the gate goes on exactly as it does today (C3: a review that failed on its own, at the current head, with no newer run, still starts its round or stops at the cap).

C2, one push. Today the `applied` step pushes the agent's commits, then `finish ready` marks the PR ready and pushes an empty `chore: ready for review` commit (review_push). In this repository (and the test repository, whose pipeline is its own caller) the `ready_for_review` event also starts a run. So a round that ends ready starts two or three pipeline runs, and the newer ones cancel the older ones' reviews. New order when the outbox's `ready` goes (ready_goes with the verify verdict):
1. Apply the other intents first. `tick` reads the subjects of the PR's commits plus the agent's local commits not yet pushed (`origin/$BRANCH..HEAD`, already checked to build on the branch).
2. `finish ready` writes "How it was tested", checks the reproduction test at the commit about to be pushed (local HEAD) rather than the PR's current head, and runs `gh pr ready`.
3. One push: the agent's commits plus a local empty `chore: ready for review` commit, through api-commit.py (signed, with the co-author trailers `autopilot.py push` adds), followed by the existing wait for the PR to show it. If that push fails, `gh pr ready --undo`, as today.

With no new local commits, review_push (the API-made empty commit) is that single push, as today. When no `ready` goes, the commits are pushed once, as today, with no ready commit.

So that the push's run is the only review here, the review job of pull-request.yml, and of org-pull-request.yml and workflow-templates/test-pull-request.yml (kept in step, tests/workflows/test_test_repo_pipeline.py), skips `ready_for_review` on dilux-bot's `autopilot` pull requests: the push that follows starts it. Other repositories' ruleset runs never fired on `ready_for_review`, so nothing changes there. This widens no permission, secret, lane or limit; it only removes one review run. The header comments of autopilot.yml and org-pull-request.yml, review_push's docstring and docs/workflows.md (#269's empty commit) say the new order.

### Spec: files

- scripts/autopilot.py (`superseded` and its command; `tick` reading the local commits; `finish ready` and `apply_outbox` with the single push; self-tests)
- .github/workflows/autopilot.yml (prep's RUN_HEAD and the superseded wait in "may"; the `applied` step's push order)
- .github/workflows/pull-request.yml (review skips an autopilot PR's `ready_for_review`)
- .github/workflows/org-pull-request.yml, workflow-templates/test-pull-request.yml (the same, kept in step)
- docs/workflows.md
- tests/workflows/test_autopilot_cancelled_review.py (new)
- tests/workflows/test_autopilot_ready_push.py (new)

### Spec: tests

- C1 → tests/workflows/test_autopilot_cancelled_review.py (the "may" step's fix gate, with gh standing in: the review job is `cancelled`, the PR's head has moved and a newer run exists, so the outputs say go=false and no `needs-human` or comment call is made)
- C2 → tests/workflows/test_autopilot_ready_push.py (apply_outbox with a tick and a `ready` that goes, with gh and api-commit.py standing in: `gh pr ready` comes before exactly one push, whose head is the `chore: ready for review` commit on top of the agent's commits; and the pipeline's review job skips `ready_for_review` on an autopilot PR)
- C3 → tests/workflows/test_autopilot_cancelled_review.py (the same gate with the review job `failure` at the current head and no newer run: the round goes on, go=true, and at the cap `needs-human` is added as today)

title: feat: the reproduction's steps leave the labels
body:
### Problem

Part 1 of #618. The reproduction still keeps its steps in labels: `bug:unconfirmed` while it waits to run, `layer:*` for where the defect shows, `could-not-reproduce` and `repro:no-way` for its outcome. A person cannot act on any of them except to give more information or take the bug over, which `needs-info` and `needs-human` already say.

### Scope

- `bug:unconfirmed` and `layer:*` are no longer set: the reproduction's step and its layer are on the issue's board (the state block of scripts/receipts.py).
- `could-not-reproduce` becomes `needs-info`, and `repro:no-way` becomes `needs-human`, each with its reason on the board.
- `bug:confirmed` stays: it is the reproduced bug's acceptance. `repro:run` and `repro:again` stay as triggers, removed as soon as they are read.
- The issues that carry the retired labels get their state on the board before the labels are removed from them.

### Out of scope

- The other parts of #618, each its own sub-issue, done one at a time in the core in the order #618 gives.
- The classification labels (`type:*`, `complexity:*`, `risk:*`, `version:*`, Dependabot's) and the bot's trigger labels, which stay.

### Acceptance criteria

- C1: Given a new bug report, when the triage and the reproduction run, then the issue never carries `bug:unconfirmed`, `layer:*`, `could-not-reproduce` or `repro:no-way`, and its board shows the reproduction's step, layer and outcome.
- C2: Given a reproduction that finds nothing, or no way to reproduce, when it ends, then the issue carries `needs-info` or `needs-human` and the board names the reason.
- C3: Given an open issue that carries one of the retired labels, when the migration runs, then its state is on its board before the label is removed.

### Criticality

Normal

🤖 AI-assisted · Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)

### Spec: approach

The reproduction's state moves from labels to one key of the board's state, `repro`, which `scripts/receipts.py state set` already writes: `{"step": ..., "layer": ..., "reason": ..., "at": ...}`. `step` is one of `waiting` (the triage called it a bug), `confirmed`, `not-reproduced`, `no-way`, `no-verdict` (today's "stays bug:unconfirmed"), `broken` or `blocked`. `layer` is one of repro-ways.py's LAYERS. `reason` is the short text the comment already gives. `scripts/receipts.py` gets a pure `repro_row(state)` that `board_text` renders as a `| Reproduction | … |` row: an icon, the step in words, the layer and the reason, passed through `clean()`. It also gets a pure `migrate(labels)` that maps the retired labels to the state, plus the labels to add and remove: `bug:unconfirmed` → step `waiting`; `layer:X` → layer X; `could-not-reproduce` → step `not-reproduced` + `needs-info`; `repro:no-way` → step `no-way` + `needs-human`.

- Triage (`scripts/triage-act.sh`, and the #606 kept-Bug step in `issue-triage.yml`): instead of adding `bug:unconfirmed` and `layer:<x>`, it runs `receipts.py state set repro='{"step":"waiting","layer":"<x>"}'`. The #496 reply stops naming the label and points to the board instead.
- Reproduction (`issue-repro.yml`): the "way" step reads the layer with `receipts.py state get repro` (default `logic`, as today). Each outcome sets the step on the board. If the stylesheet test is rejected, the layer becomes `browser` in the state instead of `layer:browser`. When nothing is found (no test written, a passing test, a browser test that failed twice), `could-not-reproduce` becomes `needs-info`, with step `not-reproduced` and the reason. When no way exists (both places), `repro:no-way` becomes `needs-human`, with step `no-way` and the reason. A limit with no verdict sets step `no-verdict` instead of re-adding `bug:unconfirmed`. A later confirmed run removes the `needs-info`/`needs-human` only when the board's step says the reproduction put it there (`not-reproduced`/`no-way`). It no longer removes `repro:no-way`. `bug:confirmed` stays. `repro:run`, `repro:again`, `repro:retry` and `repro:unblocked` are still removed as soon as they are read. `repro:broken` and `repro:blocked` are left as they are (not in this PRD). If `state set` is refused (exit 3: the board was edited by hand), the run carries on with a `::warning::`. Labels are never used as a fallback.
- Migration: a new `scripts/sync-repos.py retire-labels [--repo …] [--dry-run]` command. For each repository in repos.yml and each open issue that carries a retired label, it calls `receipts.py state set repro=…` first. Only when that exits 0 does it add `needs-info`/`needs-human` and then remove the retired labels, one call per label (#267). An issue whose state could not be written keeps its labels and is listed in the output. Like `sync-repos.py labels` today, the label definitions are not deleted: closed issues keep their history. `labels.yml` drops the 8 entries (`bug:unconfirmed`, `layer:*` ×5, `could-not-reproduce`, `repro:no-way`) and lists them in its header as retired by #801.

A choice for the maintainer: the `stale` job of `issue-triage.yml` closes a `needs-info` issue once the bot's last comment is older than `stale-days`. A migrated `could-not-reproduce` issue whose reproduction comment is old would be closed at the next sweep, with no warning to its reporter.
- (A) Leave the sweep as it is: migrated issues can close the next day.
- (B, recommended) Count the wait from the moment `needs-info` was last added, read from the issue's timeline (`labeled` event). This is also how long the issue has waited for that information. It is one small change to the stale job, tested in the new wiring test.
- (C) Have the migration post a comment that asks the reporter for what would settle it, which restarts the clock. This adds one comment per migrated issue.

### Spec: files

- scripts/receipts.py (the `repro` row, `migrate()`, docstring, `--test`)
- scripts/triage-act.sh (state in place of the labels, reply text, `--test`)
- scripts/sync-repos.py (`retire-labels`, docstring, `--test`; the 3550 label check without `bug:unconfirmed`)
- scripts/release-scenarios.py (BUG_VERDICTS and its docstring: `bug:confirmed` and `needs-info`, `needs-human` in place of `repro:no-way`)
- scripts/repro-ways.py (docstring: the layer comes from the board)
- scripts/repro-trigger.sh (its tests' `bug:unconfirmed` cases renamed to a label no longer used)
- .github/workflows/issue-triage.yml (the kept-Bug step, header, the stale job if option B)
- .github/workflows/issue-repro.yml (the way step, no-way step, report step; the App tokens that now write the board get `permission-contents: read`; header)
- .github/workflows/issues.yml (header comment)
- labels.yml
- tests/release/scenarios.yml (`bug-not-reproduced` expects `needs-info` and no retired label; `bug-reproduced` expects `repro:no-way` absent → `needs-human` absent)
- tests/workflows/test_repro_board_state.py (new)
- tests/workflows/test_reproduction_wiring.py, tests/workflows/test_maintainer_bug_wiring.py, tests/repro/test_issue_496.py (their assertions on the retired labels now apply to the board state)
- docs/workflows.md, docs/model.md, kinds/engine-test/pack.yml (comment), kinds/README.md (the layer "the triage says", on the board)

### Spec: tests

- C1 → tests/workflows/test_repro_board_state.py (no step of issue-triage.yml, issue-repro.yml or triage-act.sh adds `bug:unconfirmed`, `layer:`, `could-not-reproduce` or `repro:no-way`; the triage sets `repro` step `waiting` with its layer; the way step reads the layer from `state get repro`), scripts/triage-act.sh --test (the verdict's layer goes to `state set`, no `--add-label` of a retired label), scripts/receipts.py --test (the board's Reproduction row shows step, layer and outcome)
- C2 → tests/workflows/test_repro_board_state.py (each "found nothing" branch adds `needs-info` and each "no way" branch adds `needs-human`, both with a `state set` whose step and reason are given; a confirmed run removes them only when the step names the reproduction), scripts/receipts.py --test (the row names the reason, cleaned)
- C3 → scripts/sync-repos.py --test (`retire-labels` against a fake `gh`: the state is written before any `--remove-label`, `needs-info`/`needs-human` are added, a refused state set leaves the labels, `--dry-run` changes nothing), scripts/receipts.py --test (`migrate()` maps each retired label)

### Spec: impact

- Every DiluxOne repository's triage and reproduction (reusable workflows), which change on the next release. Callers do not change: the inputs and outputs stay the same.
- Readers of the retired labels: the layer read in issue-repro.yml, release-scenarios.py BUG_VERDICTS, the scenario `bug-not-reproduced`, the sync-repos labels test, and the wiring tests listed above. Nothing in autopilot.py, waiting.py or repro-cap.py reads them (grep).
- `needs-human` on an unconfirmed bug: autopilot.py `can_start` already stays out of an issue that carries it, which is what a no-way bug should do. `waiting.py` will list these bugs as waiting on a person, which is a new entry there that the PRD intends.
- `needs-info` on a not-reproduced bug brings it under the stale sweep (see the choice in the approach). The sweep also removes `needs-info` when someone answers, which today does not restart a reproduction: `repro:again` still does that.
- The board can now appear on an issue before acceptance, because `state set` creates it. Several jobs writing the board (triage, G1 checks, reproduction) each read, change and write it back. Two writes at the same moment can lose one, as they already can for `waits`. The layer then falls back to `logic`, as it does today when no label is set.
- A board that was edited by hand refuses `state set`: the layer falls back to `logic`, the outcome is still said in the comment and its label, and the migration skips that issue.

### Spec: threats

- Tampering: a person edits the board's state to change the layer or step. The hash check already makes `state get` exit 3 and `state set` refuse. The reproduction then uses `logic`, and the migration leaves that issue's labels in place.
- Spoofing: the state is read only from dilux-bot's own board comment (`bot_comments`). A comment by anyone else with a `dx-state` block is ignored.
- Information disclosure / injection: `reason` comes from the model's summary or repro-ways' `why`, both shaped by the issue's text. It reaches the workflow through `env:`, is put into JSON by `jq`/Python (never by shell interpolation), shown through `clean()` (no pipes, no mentions, one line, 200 characters), and stored through `state_block`, which escapes `<`, `>` and `--`.
- Elevation of privilege: the App tokens that write the board gain `permission-contents: read` on their own repository, which the board needs to read the seal. This widening is stated in the pull request. No secret, lane or limit changes. The migration runs with the token of whoever runs sync-repos.py (a maintainer, or org-drift's App) and only edits labels and the bot's board comment.
- Denial of service: `retire-labels` lists at most 100 issues per label per repository (`--limit`, as the stale job does) and can be run again. It is idempotent: an issue with no retired label is left alone.
- Repudiation: the old labels' meaning goes into the state with `at`, and the migration prints every issue it changed or skipped.

### Spec: architecture

The state goes in the board's existing state block (#564) through `receipts.py state get/set`. There is no new store or comment. The row and the migration mapping are pure functions in receipts.py, tested in its `--test`, like `waits_row`. The organisation-wide migration is a `sync-repos.py` mode, alongside `labels`, that reads repos.yml and keeps `--dry-run`. Workflows pass untrusted text through `env:` and keep one label per `gh issue edit` call (#267). It must not break: `bug:confirmed` and the `bugfix-reproduced` lane that follows it, the `repro:run`/`repro:again` triggers and their removal, the #496 kept-Bug path and the maintainer's own Bug path (#564: no reproduction), `repro:retry`/`repro:broken`/`repro:blocked`, and the release scenarios' preconditions (#707).

title: feat: the triage keeps its verdicts and drops its steps
body:
### Problem

Part 3 of #618. The triage marks a step no one acts on (`needs-triage`, which the triage itself removes minutes later), `needs:maintainer` says the same as `needs-human`, and GitHub's default `enhancement` and `bug` repeat what the native issue Type already says.

### Scope

- `needs-triage` is no longer set: the board says whether the triage has run.
- `needs:maintainer` merges into `needs-human` (scripts/run-issue.sh and the workflows that set it).
- `enhancement` and `bug` are no longer set nor created by scripts/sync-repos.py, and are removed from the issues that carry them once their Type is set.
- The triage's verdicts stay as labels: `by-design`, `duplicate`, `question`, `planned`, `pro-feature`, `exists-in-pro`, `spike`, `needs-info`.

### Out of scope

- The other parts of #618, each its own sub-issue, done one at a time in the core in the order #618 gives.
- The classification labels (`type:*`, `complexity:*`, `risk:*`, `version:*`, Dependabot's) and the bot's trigger labels, which stay.

### Acceptance criteria

- C1: Given a new issue, when the triage runs, then it never carries `needs-triage`, and its board says the triage ran.
- C2: Given a recurring run that needs a person, when scripts/run-issue.sh opens its issue, then it carries `needs-human`, not `needs:maintainer`.
- C3: Given an open issue that carries `enhancement` or `bug`, when the migration runs, then its native Type is set to Feature or Bug before the label is removed, and scripts/sync-repos.py no longer creates either label.

### Criticality

Normal

🤖 AI-assisted · Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)

### Spec: approach

The PRD passes G1: the problem is clear, and every criterion can be tested with the scripts' self-tests and the workflow tests.

1. **`needs-triage` (C1).** Nothing sets it any more. `scripts/triage-act.sh` and the two fallback steps of `issue-triage.yml` ("over the cap", "Say the triage could not run") write the outcome into the board's state instead, as one `triage` key: `{"ran": true, "verdict": "<category>", "at": "<UTC>"}`, or `{"ran": false, "why": "cap|failed|no-verdict|unknown"}`. They write it with `receipts.py state set`, the #564 state block. `receipts.py board_text` adds a `| Triage | … |` row from that key: "✓ ran at <time>: <verdict label>", or "✗ could not run (<why>): a maintainer re-runs the job or triages it by hand". `act()` calls `board_upsert` on the normal path too, so every triaged issue gets a board. Two options for what marks a triage that did not run, which a maintainer may care about:
   - **(A, recommended)** The board alone: the ✗ row, plus the board's "Waits on" row set to the maintainer (`receipts.py waits`), so the one mention per step tells them. No label. The failure comment says "its board says so" instead of "waits as `needs-triage`".
   - (B) `needs-human` on such an issue. This puts the triage's own failure into the label that means "the autopilot handed this over", which is the overlap the PRD removes.
   Either way the label-creation loop in `act()`, the `gh label create needs-triage` calls and `--remove-label needs-triage` stop using it. `issue-accepted.yml` keeps removing it only so that issues that still carry an old `needs-triage` lose it (no new one is set).
2. **`needs:maintainer` → `needs-human` (C2).** `scripts/run-issue.sh` (`labels_for`, and `settle`'s query) and the spike step of `issue-triage.yml` set and read `needs-human`. The label's entry comes out of `labels.yml`, and the comment headers of `runner-image.yml`, `autonomy-digest.yml` and `issue-triage.yml` change with it.
3. **`enhancement` / `bug` (C3).**
   - `labels.yml` loses `enhancement`. `bug` was never in it; this is now asserted in `sync-repos.py --test`.
   - The `labels: [...]` line goes from `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml` and `feature_request.yml`, which already set `type:`.
   - `triage-act.sh` no longer adds `enhancement`. The Feature Type carries it; `exists-in-pro` is still added alone when the verdict says so. An empty label list adds nothing. The verdict's internal category name `enhancement` stays, because `triage-reply.sh`, `repro-trigger.sh` and the JSON schema read it.
   - The migration goes in `scripts/sync-repos.py` as a function `retire_labels(repo, dry)`. For each open issue carrying `enhancement`, `bug` or `needs:maintainer`:
     - no Type → PATCH `type=Feature|Bug`, read it back, and only then remove the label;
     - a Type already set → the Type is kept (#341) and the label is removed;
     - both `bug` and `enhancement` and no Type → left alone and reported;
     - `needs:maintainer` → `needs-human` is added, then `needs:maintainer` is removed.
     It never deletes a label from a repository, in line with `labels`' "never deletes one". Two options for when it runs:
   - **(A, recommended)** Inside `labels`, after `sync_labels`, so `all` and the daily `org-drift.yml` run it. It is idempotent and does nothing once no open issue carries these labels. It also catches issues still opened from a repository's own stale form.
   - (B) Its own subcommand `retire-labels`, run once by hand. That is less to read in every daily run, but nothing catches a straggler.

### Spec: files

- scripts/triage-act.sh (its `--test` too)
- scripts/receipts.py (the Triage row in `board_text`; its `--test`)
- scripts/run-issue.sh (its `--test`)
- scripts/sync-repos.py (`retire_labels`, wired into `labels`; its `--test`; the needs-triage assertion near line 3550)
- .github/workflows/issue-triage.yml
- .github/workflows/issue-accepted.yml (comment only)
- .github/workflows/runner-image.yml, .github/workflows/autonomy-digest.yml (header comments)
- .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml, .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.yml
- labels.yml
- tests/workflows/test_triage_non_write_users.py
- tests/workflows/test_issue_803_labels.py (new)
- docs/workflows.md, docs/maintaining.md, docs/plans/autonomy.md, README/CONTRIBUTING wherever they name these labels
- CHANGELOG is left to the release

### Spec: tests

- C1 → tests/workflows/test_issue_803_labels.py, which checks:
  - the triage steps of `issue-triage.yml` never add `needs-triage`;
  - `triage-act.sh act` with a fake `gh` writes the `triage` state and never `needs-triage`, for a verdict, no verdict and an unknown category;
  - `board_text` shows the Triage row.

  Also scripts/triage-act.sh `--test`, scripts/receipts.py `--test`, and tests/workflows/test_triage_non_write_users.py updated.
- C2 → scripts/run-issue.sh `--test` (the labels carry `needs-human`, never `needs:maintainer`; `settle` queries `needs-human`), and test_issue_803_labels.py for the spike step.
- C3 → scripts/sync-repos.py `--test`, which checks:
  - `retire_labels` with a fake `gh`: the PATCH of Type comes before the label's removal, an existing Type is kept, an issue with both labels is left alone, `needs:maintainer` moves to `needs-human`, and a failed PATCH keeps the label;
  - `labels.yml` holds neither `enhancement` nor `bug`.

  Also test_issue_803_labels.py, which checks that the issue forms set no `bug`/`enhancement` label.

### Spec: impact

- Every DiluxOne repository: the triage, the run issues and the daily label sync reach all of them.
- **Readers of the retired labels.** Searches or saved views of `needs:maintainer` (docs/plans/autonomy.md names a Project view) must use `needs-human`, and the docs change with them.
- **`needs-human` gets more meanings.** It now also marks run issues and answered spikes. `autopilot.py may_continue` refuses pull requests carrying it; it reads the pull request's labels, not the issue's, so issue-level `needs-human` does not block an accepted issue's autopilot (issue-repro.yml already sets it on issues).
- **The board.** It gains one row. Its state block keeps its hash scheme, and the new key is additive.
- **The migration.** It writes to issues in every repository, one PATCH per issue the first time, then nothing.
- **What it can break.**
  - The triage's tests that assert `needs-triage`: they are updated.
  - `sync-repos.py`'s check that `needs-triage` is among the labels: it is updated.
  - An issue opened from a repository's own copy of the old form still gets `bug`/`enhancement` until the migration runs. That copy is a finding, not part of this change.
- **Sibling code that labels the same way.** The repro labels (`bug:unconfirmed`, `bug:confirmed`) are left as they are.

### Spec: threats

- **Spoofing.** The migration and the triage act with dilux-bot's token, as today. The triage state is written only to dilux-bot's own board comment, and only that comment is read (#564).
- **Tampering.** A person editing the board's block by hand makes it read as edited, so nothing is set on it. An issue's text never reaches the migration's shell: Python's argv lists only, with no shell interpolation. The workflow steps keep passing untrusted text through `env:`.
- **Repudiation.** Each Type change is in the issue's timeline under dilux-bot.
- **Information disclosure.** None new: labels and Types are already public on their issues, and the board shows a category, never the paid roadmap.
- **Denial of service.** The migration pages open issues per label (`--limit` with pagination) and stops at the first API error per repository, reporting it. A failed PATCH never removes a label.
- **Elevation of privilege.** No permission, secret, lane or limit is widened. Setting an issue's Type and its labels needs `issues: write`, which the label sync and the triage tokens already hold. Removing `needs-triage` from the flow opens no path to acceptance.

### Spec: architecture

The triage's outcome becomes data on the board's state (#564, `receipts.py state set`), the pattern every other step already uses, not a label. The migration is one more function of `scripts/sync-repos.py` next to `sync_labels`, tested in its `--test` with the fake `gh` its other tests use. The label list stays in `labels.yml` as data. It must not break:
- `labels`' rule of never deleting a label;
- the board's hash and its "edited by hand" handling;
- the verdict category names that `triage-reply.sh` and `repro-trigger.sh` read;
- #341/#496 (a Type a maintainer set is kept);
- `run-issue.sh settle` finding open issues that waited on a person before the change (the migration relabels them to `needs-human`).

title: fix: accepting a bug already reproduced opens a second pull request
body:
### What happened?

Bug #798 was reproduced (`bug:confirmed`, `tests/repro/test_issue_798.py`), and the `bugfix-reproduced` lane opened #799, "The bug reproduced from #798", whose autopilot opened #800. A few minutes later a maintainer added `accepted` to #798 itself, and the autopilot started on #798 as well and opened #806, a second pull request for the same fix with the same files. Two autopilot runs and two reviews were paid for one bug, and #806 had to be closed by hand as a duplicate.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a bug that the reproduction confirms: the lane opens "The bug reproduced from #N" and its autopilot opens a pull request.
2. Add `accepted` to the original report #N.
3. The autopilot starts on #N too and opens a second pull request for it.

### Version

v7.14.1 (main at 58cf115)

### Proposed solution

When `accepted` is added to a bug whose reproduction already handed it to the `bugfix-reproduced` lane (`bug:confirmed` with an open "The bug reproduced from #N" issue, or a pull request already working it), the autopilot does not start: the acceptance is recorded, and the bot answers on the report, once, with the link to the lane's issue and pull request that already fix it. The same check covers any accepted issue that already has an open autopilot pull request closing it.

### Problem

Accepting a bug the reproduction already confirmed starts a second autopilot on the same fix, so two pull requests compete for one bug, the reviews are paid twice, and a person has to close one of them.

### Scope

- Before the autopilot starts on an accepted issue, it checks whether the `bugfix-reproduced` lane already took it (an open "The bug reproduced from #N" issue) or an open pull request already closes it, and then does not start.
- The bot's answer on the report, once, linking where the fix already is.
- A test that would have caught it, in the autopilot's `--test` or a reproduction test.

### Out of scope

- Who may add `accepted`, and what the reproduction lane does.

### Acceptance criteria

- C1: Given a bug whose reproduction opened "The bug reproduced from #N" and whose fix pull request is open, when a maintainer adds `accepted` to #N, then no second autopilot run starts and no second pull request is opened.
- C2: Given that case, when the acceptance is skipped, then the bot comments once on #N with the links to the lane's issue and its pull request.
- C3: Given an accepted issue with no lane issue and no open pull request closing it, when the autopilot runs, then it starts as it does today.

### Criticality

Normal

🤖 AI-generated · Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)

### Spec: approach

A new check, run in `prep`'s "May it start" step of `.github/workflows/autopilot.yml` right after `holder` and only on a start (`AS=start`; a continue already has its pull request), says whether the fix already lives elsewhere: `NUMBER=<n> python3 .dx-central/scripts/autopilot.py taken`. It exits 0 when nothing took the issue (the run goes on as today, C3), 1 when something did (`go=false`, no spec, no draft, no second pull request: C1), and 2 when GitHub could not be read (fails closed, as `holder` does, with the same kind of comment).

The decision is a pure function `taken_by(number, lanes, prs)` in `scripts/autopilot.py`. `lanes` are the open issues labelled `lane:bugfix-reproduced`, each with its title, author and the open pull requests that close it (GitHub's closing link). The function keeps only those whose title is exactly "The bug reproduced from #<n>" and whose author is dilux-bot (`BOT_LOGINS`): a person can copy the title, but nothing they write takes an issue away from the autopilot. `prs` are the open pull requests that close #n by GitHub's link (the `closedByPullRequestsReferences` that `read_holder` already reads), whoever wrote them. A person's pull request opened earlier is already `held_by`'s case and stays its case. The function returns the links: the lane's issue and its open pull request(s), or the pull request(s) that close #n, or nothing. A `read_taken(repo, number)` makes one GraphQL read for both: the lane issues by label with their closing pull requests, and the issue's own closing pull requests.

When the result is not empty, the step comments on #n once (C2), through `taken_comment(links)`. The comment starts with the marker `dx-autopilot-taken` (in an HTML comment) and names the lane's issue and its pull request ("The fix is already on its way: #L, the `bugfix-reproduced` lane's issue for this report, and its pull request #P. The autopilot does not start a second one.") with the AI line. Before it posts, `taken` reads the issue's comments and posts nothing if dilux-bot already wrote one with that marker. A second acceptance, or a re-run, adds no second comment. When the lane has no pull request yet, the comment links the lane's issue alone. The issue's board is refreshed as usual.

The check is made only before the autopilot starts, as the PRD says. It does not go into `holder`, which `draft` and `apply` also run mid-run: a lane issue that appears after a run started does not stop that run. Nothing changes in who may add `accepted` or in what the reproduction lane does. No permission, secret, lane or limit is widened: the step uses the token and the reads `prep` already has (issues and pull requests, read; issue comments, write).

The workflow header comment of autopilot.yml, the usage block of scripts/autopilot.py, and the docs that describe when the autopilot steps aside (docs/workflows.md, docs/agents.md) get one sentence each on this case.

### Spec: files

- scripts/autopilot.py (`taken_by`, `read_taken`, `taken_comment`, the `taken` command, its usage line, and its cases in `--test`)
- .github/workflows/autopilot.yml (the call in prep's "May it start", on a start only, and its header comment)
- docs/workflows.md
- docs/agents.md
- changelog fragment for the change (as the repository's changelog-fragments.sh expects)

### Spec: tests

- C1 → scripts/autopilot.py (`--test`: `taken_by` finds dilux-bot's open "The bug reproduced from #N" issue and its open pull request, and an open pull request that closes #N. A person's issue with the same title, a closed lane issue, and the title of another report's lane issue do not count. The workflow check confirms prep runs `autopilot.py taken` after `holder`, before the lane and the spec, on a start only, and ends with `go=false` when it exits non-zero.)
- C2 → scripts/autopilot.py (`--test`: `taken_comment` carries the marker, the links to the lane's issue and its pull request, and the AI line. Given comments that already hold dilux-bot's marker, the `taken` command posts nothing. A marker in a person's comment does not count. The gh calls are faked.)
- C3 → scripts/autopilot.py (`--test`: with no lane issue for #N and no open pull request that closes it, `taken_by` returns nothing and `taken` exits 0 without commenting. The workflow check confirms the step goes on to `lane` and `may-start` as today.)

title: fix: the review set is graded on the bug's line
body:
### What happened?

The review's golden set (evals/review/, scripts/review-eval.py) labels a case "flag" when a review thread later went outdated or resolved (review-eval.py:73), counts any blocker or major on the same file as found (:128-137), has 4 of its 6 clean cases from bot sync pull requests, passes the gate at 2 of 6 with a slack of 1, and keeps a 3/6 baseline written once (#246) while runs swing (run 44407091670 scored 4/6). The weekly digest's "fixed" (scripts/review-outcomes.py) uses the same outdated-or-resolved rule.

### Steps to reproduce

Read evals/review/cases.json, scripts/review-eval.py `verdict` and `score`, and run 44407091670.

### Version

v7.18.0

### Proposed solution

A flag case records its known bug's file and line, and enters the set only when the commit that fixed it changed that line (checked from git, no person). A flag counts as found only when a blocker or major names that file within 3 lines of it. Clean cases are real merged pull requests that changed code and needed no later fix, at most one from a bot. The set grows to 10 flag and 10 clean cases, each run is played 3 times and scored by the median, and the baseline is rewritten from that. The digest counts a finding as fixed only when the commit that changed its line was in reply to it and the pull request merged with no later fix of that line.

### Problem

The review's score can reward an invented finding and an easy clean set, so it does not show whether the review finds bugs.

### Scope

- evals/review/cases.json and baseline.json, scripts/review-eval.py (or evals.py's review step), scripts/review-outcomes.py, with `--test` cases.

### Out of scope

- The review's prompt.

### Acceptance criteria

- C1: Given the review set, when it is validated, then every flag case's line was changed by the commit that fixed it, and a case that was not is refused by its name.
- C2: Given a review that flags a different line of the same file, when it is scored, then the case counts as missed.
- C3: Given the set's run, when it is scored, then it holds at least 10 flag and 10 clean cases, plays each 3 times and scores the median.

### Criticality

Normal

🤖 AI-generated · Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)

### Spec: approach

The PRD is clear and each criterion can be tested: C1 is a validator with a refusal that names the case, C2 is how `verdict` decides, and C3 is the set's size, the number of plays and the median.

- **Cases carry a line and a fix (C1).** Each `flag` case in `evals/review/cases.json` gets `line` (the thread's `originalLine` at `head`) and `fix` (the commit of the pull request that changed that line). `collect` reads `originalLine` and the pull request's commits from GraphQL, then uses git in a clone. It walks the commits after `head` and picks the first one where `git diff -U0 <head> <commit> -- <path>` changes that line, meaning the line falls inside a `-a,b` hunk with b ≥ 1. A thread that is only outdated, where no commit changed its line, is not a flag case. A new `review-eval.py check` step clones each case's repository, which is public, and refuses any flag case with no `line` or `fix`, or whose line `fix` did not change. It exits 1 and names each refused case (`<id>: line N of <path> was not changed by <fix>`). `run` does this check first and stops before any paid review.
- **The line must match (C2).** `verdict` counts a flag case as found only when a new blocker or major points at the case's `path` and `line`. A finding on another line of the same file, or with no line, counts as missed. There are two options:
  - A (recommended): the exact line, which is what C2 says.
  - B: any line in the hunk the fix changed. This is kinder to a model that points one line off, but a different line can then pass, and that goes against C2 as written.
- **The set and the median (C3).** Two constants: `MIN_CASES = 10` of each kind and `PLAYS = 3`. `run` and `score` refuse a set with fewer than 10 `flag` or 10 `clean` cases. `run` reviews each case 3 times, with a fresh `last.json` and a fresh checkout each time, and records the three results per case. `score` takes the median per case: found or blocked when 2 of 3 plays say so. Plays that could not be reviewed are dropped, and a case with fewer than 2 reviewed plays counts as unreviewed. The table shows each case's three plays. There are two options for what "the median" means:
  - A (recommended): the median per case, as above. It is robust to one odd answer, and the table still says which case moved.
  - B: the median of the three plays' set totals.
- **The data.** `collect` is called with 10 (the default becomes 10) to rewrite `cases.json` with at least 10 of each kind. The baseline is then rewritten from a whole 3-play run in the new format. This has two requirements the work step may not have:
  - a GitHub read token for `collect`'s GraphQL search;
  - a paid run of 20 cases × 3 = 60 reviews (today: 12) for `baseline`.

  Options:
  - A (recommended): `review-eval.yml` gets a `workflow_dispatch` input `mode: collect`. It runs `collect` and then a whole run with `GITHUB_TOKEN` (contents: read, which can read the public repositories), and uploads `cases.json` and `baseline.json` as the artifact. The autopilot then commits them to this pull request.
  - B: a maintainer runs `collect 10` and `baseline` locally and gives the files to the pull request.
- **Limits this widens, for the person who merges.** The paid evaluation grows from 12 to 60 reviews per run. To stay within the job's time, `review-eval.yml` runs the 3 plays as a 3-job matrix (`run --play N`, `timeout-minutes: 180` each, up from 120 for one job). A fourth job scores the merged results. Nothing else changes: no new secret, permission or lane.
- `scripts/review-outcomes.py` stays as it is, because no criterion asks it to change. It still counts an outdated thread as fixed even when its line did not change (see the findings in the pull request).

### Spec: files

- scripts/review-eval.py (collect with line and fix, `check`, the line-exact `verdict`, `MIN_CASES`/`PLAYS`, the median `score`, `run --play`, its `--test` cases)
- evals/review/cases.json (≥10 flag with `line` and `fix`, ≥10 clean)
- evals/review/baseline.json (from a whole 3-play run, the median)
- .github/workflows/review-eval.yml (the check first, a matrix of 3 plays, a scoring job, the `collect` dispatch mode, the header comment)
- docs/workflows.md (the review-eval.yml and review-eval.py rows)
- tests/workflows/test_review_eval_line.py
- tests/workflows/test_review_eval_set.py

### Spec: tests

- C1 → tests/workflows/test_review_eval_line.py
- C2 → tests/workflows/test_review_eval_line.py
- C3 → tests/workflows/test_review_eval_set.py
